Definition: a fortified place; figuratively, a defence
BiblicalUsage: The word names a fortress, a stronghold, and it is the refuge of the psalms. David says God is his strength and power and makes his way perfect, and the psalm says the LORD is his light and his salvation, and the strength of his life, of whom shall he be afraid. He asks God to be his strong rock, a house of defence to save him, and Isaiah says the LORD is a strength to the poor and a refuge from the storm.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the fortress is not a place but a Person, because David's strength was God Himself and not the walls around him. I hold that the poor and the needy find their stronghold in the same LORD, and no storm can take the house whose rock is God.
